description.text: Derrick de Kerckhove is a sociologist and academic who has spent most of his career exploring the intersection of culture, technology, and media. He earned a Ph.D. in philosophy and French literature from the University of Toronto in 1975 and a second Ph.D. in the sociology of art from the University of Tours in 1979, after which he became a long‑time associate of the Centre for Culture and Technology and worked closely with Marshall McLuhan for more than a decade as translator, assistant, and co‑author.

From 1983 to 2008 he directed the McLuhan Program in Culture & Technology at the University of Toronto, while also teaching at the University of Naples Federico II and the Universitas Mercatorum. His scholarship includes the influential book *The Skin of Culture and Connected Intelligence*, which extends Pierre Lévy’s theory of collective intelligence to the digital network context, and the concept of a “brainframe,” describing how digital technologies reshape deep cognitive organization.

curiosities.text: He introduced the concept of a brainframe, a deep cognitive architecture of the brain that is altered by the use of digital technologies.
He worked with Marshall McLuhan for over ten years, serving as translator, assistant, and co‑author on several projects.
In 2026 he acquired Italian citizenship after many years of residence and academic activity in Italy.
